still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived; Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Off-drug arithmetic: 31.5% ever − 23.1% current = 8.4% of adults who used and are off now. 45% of ever-users have cycled = 14.2 pts: ~11.7 pts are current users on at least a second course (~51% of current users) and ~2.5 pts cycled and are off again; the remaining ~5.9 pts stopped once and never restarted (down from 6.1 as some of that group restarted, mainly on cheap orals or gray vials). Consistent with one-year persistence near one-third and 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×14 + 0.33×24.3 + 0.24×34 + 0.23×18 = 2.8 + 8.02 + 8.16 + 4.14 ≈ 23.1. Income thirds average (26+24+19)/3 ≈ 23. ~270M adults × 23.1% ≈ 62.4M users. Payer mix: commercial ~12.5M (20%; includes ~5.2M in monitored metabolic tracks), Medicare ~11.6M (18.6%; ~9.6M aged 65+ plus ~2M disability-eligible), Medicaid ~3.6M (5.8%), legitimate cash (TrumpRx/manufacturer direct) ~26.0M (41.7%), imported or counterfeit ~8.7M (13.9%, up from 5.2M). Users 65+: 18% × ~62M ≈ 11.2M, of whom ~1.6M pay cash. The income gap narrowed (top-to-bottom 26 vs 19), but only because bottom-third growth is mostly gray-market vials at $15–40 and $149 starter pills. Top-third growth slowed as the upper tier moved to low-dose, 'off-season' and holiday patterns. 65+ growth slowed after the fracture data and the dementia sNDA refusal. Adult obesity ~32.8%; ~21% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s, ~3.0% of 12–17s. Use among 6–11s slipped from ~0.20% to ~0.18% as five states imposed under-12 limits, and most of those children are in commercially insured households in non-restricting states.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~11.6M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 11.6M × ~$250 average net/month × 12 ≈ $34.8B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before the rebate true-up (2030: $29.7B). Net price did not fall in the window, so growth is all volume. Dementia route: ~1.9M × ~$260 × 12 ≈ $5.9B. It stays on the original CVD-plus-obesity label because the Nov 2031 complete response letter blocked the extension. Medicaid: 7 states (down from 9) still cover weight-loss use at the $245 rate; ~3.6M Medicaid users are mostly on diabetes codes. CMS added DXA coverage for Part D incretin users aged 65+ in 2032.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $5–35 a month across 90+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue products are sold across Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Gulf. Canadian generics run CAD 55–95. India's regulator suspended export licences for 14 brands after the Sep 2031 contamination outbreak, and others filled the gap within months.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. TrumpRx maintenance has been frozen since 2029 levels (Wegovy pill $249; Foundayo $149–279; injectable Zepbound/Wegovy $279–349), starting orals $149, MariTide direct $299. Retatrutide 12 mg: $1,299 list, Lilly direct cash $549, allocation-limited. Amycretin: $1,250 list, ~$399 direct. Novo's Mar 2031 patent settlements set US generic semaglutide entry no earlier than mid-2033, and Lilly cites retatrutide fill-finish capacity as the reason for no further cuts. Employer coverage for weight management fell 36% → 28% (Business Group on Health, late 2031). Another ~12% of employers cover only through adherence-verified metabolic tracks (~5.2M enrollees, inside the ~12.5M commercial users), most of them on clinic-administered monthly MariTide. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, OSA and dementia codes with BMI ≥35/40 floors. Orals are ~48% of users, the result of cash buying and holiday-friendly dosing. The gray market (~8.7M) runs on Indian vials, counterfeit serialised-looking pens, and 'reta' research peptides. Demand for 'reta' is fed by people below the new BMI ≥35 floor for the 12 mg dose.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide; 12 mg high-dose tier approved Jun 2031 under REMS)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Jan 2031)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Jun 2029)

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing). The extension to adults 60+ without CVD received a complete response letter in Nov 2031
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs (oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 positive 2031; sNDA filed Mar 2032, decision 2033)
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid, now dampened by fracture data
microdosing and 'floor dosing' for steadiness without flatness
planned drug holidays (weekends on orals, skipped months on MariTide)
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label; now barred in five states)
gray 'reta' research peptide at 12 mg-equivalent doses by people below the REMS BMI floor
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The ~30% triple-agonist driver is realised by an existing product in a new form: Lilly's sNDA for a retatrutide 12 mg tier (TRIUMPH data, ~28–29% mean loss at 80 weeks) was approved Jun 2031 under a REMS (BMI ≥35 with comorbidity or ≥40, in-person initiation, baseline DXA for 60+, dysesthesia and lean-mass counselling). No new triple-agonist molecule reached market. Amycretin (filed Oct 2029) was approved Jan 2031 at ~22%. No new indication in the window: the tirzepatide dementia extension got a CRL in Nov 2031 citing fracture risk and the absence of confirmatory data, and oral semaglutide for AUD was filed Mar 2032 with a decision in 2033. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts reported phase 3 in 2032 and have not been filed. Implant programmes are still phase 1. No US generic semaglutide or tirzepatide; Novo's settlements set entry no earlier than mid-2033. Global incretin market ~$175B (2031). US net prices are flat.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide 12 mg and MariTide carry the highest early GI rates. Persistent diarrhoea in long-term users now routinely triggers elastase testing.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Higher on retatrutide 12 mg.
No causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now runs mainly on exocrine claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; new MDL consolidating exocrine-insufficiency claims formed 2031.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now recognised as a population problem. The Medicare cohort holds the hip-fracture HR at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Retatrutide 12 mg trials show ~35–40% of weight lost as lean mass without training. DXA studies show accelerated BMD loss in perimenopausal women on drug >3 years. A CDC MMWR (Nov 2031) reports the age-adjusted hip-fracture hospitalisation rate in adults 65+ rose ~4% from 2028 to 2031, reversing a decades-long decline. The report attributes most of the excess to incretin users. Sarcopenia diagnoses in Part D users roughly doubled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning strengthened (Feb 2032): baseline and biennial DXA advised for users 60+ and anyone on continuous therapy >3 years. CMS covers DXA for 65+ users. The retatrutide 12 mg REMS requires baseline DXA at 60+. The fracture data were cited in the dementia-extension CRL.

safety_ledger.effect: Stress fractures in young, physically active users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Army analysis of the recruit oral pilot found stress-fracture rates ~1.6× matched recruits during basic training. Small numbers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Army paused the recruit pilot in Aug 2031; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the FDA postmarketing mood study.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (n≈118k, reported Apr 2032) finds clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~8% of users vs ~3% of controls. It is dose-related, ~12% on retatrutide 12 mg, and most resolves within 8–12 weeks of dose reduction. It is an association, not randomised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 'Emotional blunting / anhedonia' added to adverse reactions across the class (May 2032); prescribers advised to screen at titration. Not a boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Fastest after abrupt gray-market stops following batch recalls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users, plus fat-soluble vitamin deficiency linked to exocrine insufficiency. Both are now recognised as contributors to the bone wave.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panels added to label language (2031).

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Replicated a third time (UK CPRD, 2031) at ~2× controls after year 5. Partial recovery of elastase in about half of patients 12 months after stopping. The first tirzepatide 5-year data (2032) show a smaller excess (~1.5×) with wide intervals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added to semaglutide Warnings (Mar 2031). EMA PRAC recommended class labelling; the FDA class decision for other agents is still pending.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric bone interim (liraglutide 6–11) shows slightly lower BMD gain vs reference curves, not yet significant. Cycling is linked to both fracture and regain penalties.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue. Five states restrict under-12 prescribing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: In Sep 2031 the CDC linked 287 bacteraemia and injection-site abscess cases (Burkholderia cepacia complex) in 23 states, 11 of them fatal, to vials from two Indian export brands sold through social shops. Separately, mislabelled 'reta' research vials (10× concentration) caused dozens of severe vomiting and dehydration admissions. Cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~27,000. Poison-centre calls are ~6× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA/CBP mail blitz, with seizures up ~60% on 2030. India suspended 14 export licences. FTC actions against social shops. Personal importation is still largely unenforced at the user level.

food_and_beverage.state: About 40% of US households now include a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~11% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. Dollar sales are flat because prices did not fall. The aisle has split three ways: protein and fibre lines for users; value packs for regainers; and a new premium 'full-appetite' tier (butter, heritage bread, whole-fat dairy) bought by upper-income households performing unmedicated eating. Protein ingredients are still in shortage pricing, now also driven by sarcopenia clinics prescribing protein.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~13% from 2025 and beer ~8%. Off-label AUD use via EAPs continues ahead of the 2033 decision. Mid-sized Midwestern bar closures continue. A small upscale revival of wine bars in coastal cities rides the 'appetite' aesthetic and is too small to move the totals.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Casual dining checks are smaller still. Upscale restaurants in Brooklyn, LA and Austin report the first cover growth in years from 'full table' supper-club formats, while buffets and mid-tier chains keep closing. QSR value menus grow in lower-income markets where regain is common.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting. Fitted athletic 'structured' wear is still the premium category, and designers now cut for heavier, muscular bodies ('strong sizing') at the top end. Resale and stretch serve cyclers and regainers.

fitness.state: Strength training, DXA and sarcopenia programmes grow fastest. Medicare Advantage plans contract with gym chains for resistance training for incretin users 65+. Premium clubs sell 'clean panel' memberships bundling DXA, coaching and a quarterly drug-free blood assay at $300–450 a month.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management fell to 28%. Coverage sits on diabetes, cardiac, OSA and dementia codes behind prior authorisation and BMI floors. Metabolic tracks with adherence differentials hold ~5.2M enrollees. Pharmacy trend ~+8% because net price stopped falling while volume grew. Part D premiums rose again, and plans cite incretins and new DXA/fracture costs.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on retatrutide 12 mg, which is allocation-limited; Novo holds semaglutide pricing behind its 2033 generic settlements; Amgen grows MariTide in employer clinics. Revenue grows on volume at flat net prices. Fracture litigation and the exocrine MDL are new reserve lines. Indian and Chinese makers still dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin no longer signals much because it is cheap: a $149 pill or a $20 vial produces it. Thin and soft now reads as cash or mail-order. Lean and lifted still reads as upper tier, but the new scarce body is visibly fed: muscular, a little heavy, eating in public, with a blood test to prove nothing is in it. 'Natty' (borrowed from bodybuilding) and 'clean panel' are the words.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Brooklyn and Silver Lake, upper-income women aged 30–45 announce their 'off-season' and post clean-panel results, a $180 LC-MS assay that detects semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide. Many of them actually floor-dose between tests. In Charlotte's banks, DXA printouts are still shared, but heavy lean mass now beats low body fat. On the Columbus logistics corridor, the monthly-clinic body is thin and soft and carries no prestige. Bottom-third regainers aged 50–64 are still the most visible off-drug group, joined by younger gray-market users who quit after the 2031 contamination scare.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In the upper tier the shared meal is coming back as display: long dinners, bread on the table, clearing your plate as a statement. Elsewhere meals are still short and protein-forward. 'Bread Alone' fasting churches hold ~550 congregations, and the irony that their poor members fast while the rich feast for show is a staple of sermons. School lunch fights now centre on state under-12 laws.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Premium app tiers replaced 'lean-mass verified' with 'clean panel' badges. 'On', 'off' and 'off-season' markers are standard. Couples' therapists report drug holidays as routine negotiation, scheduled around anniversaries and holidays.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become a status good in the upper tier: wanting food, drink and sex is evidence that you could afford not to need the drug. In lower-income communities appetite still reads as lost access, or as defiance. Unmuted has split again between a class-politics wing and a lifestyle wing whose 'appetite nights' are now sponsored by restaurant groups.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA study puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~12% on retatrutide 12 mg. Survey data (2032) find ~40% of long-term users have titrated below their maximum dose at least once for mood, and ~25% of oral users take planned holidays.
interior_life.framing: Everyone now calls it 'going flat'. Clinicians call it a labelled, dose-related adverse reaction and manage it with dose-down titration. Most large HR departments have dropped 'steadiness' from competency language since the May 2032 label change. Unmuted's class wing says the label proves the point and that the tracks still pay people to stay flat.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence-verified tracks (~5.2M) persist under the 2027 guidance. Holidays have become normal, and the tracks have not adjusted: a skipped clinic month forfeits the premium differential, often $150–250 a month. Some Columbus-corridor employers added a 'clinician-approved dose-down' code after grievances; others did not. One of the two EEOC ADA charges reached a cause finding in early 2032 and is in conciliation; the other is still pending. White-collar firms treat dose management as private.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Going flat' memoirs and a network sitcom about a couple on alternating holidays are mainstream. The flat-fiction imprint folded into a general list. Appetite nights spread from Detroit and Baltimore to brand-sponsored versions in Brooklyn. Sportsbook handle per account recovered slightly in holiday-heavy months, which analysts now track.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Drug holidays are the normal tool for desire mismatch, easy on orals and costly on clinic-administered monthly doses. Therapists report couples choosing pills over shots for that reason. 'Parallel lives' complaints are concentrated among metabolic-track enrollees.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Restriction, not access, moved legislatures. MAHA-aligned governors and parents' groups passed under-12 limits in five states, and HHS moved against broadcast and influencer advertising. Candidates in several 2032 races advertised being 'off' or 'clean'. The premium-differential coalition remains stalled, though the EEOC finding gave it a new talking point. There is still no turnout evidence for a 'sedated electorate'.

state.regulatory_posture: Split. The FDA stays fast on routine approvals (amycretin, retatrutide 12 mg) but uses REMS and labelling more: the 12 mg BMI floor and in-person initiation, a strengthened bone warning, the anhedonia label and the exocrine warning. It refused the dementia extension. HHS's Jan 2032 rule removes obesity drugs from the 'adequate provision' pathway, which ends broadcast DTC ads; the FTC targets telehealth influencer promotion. PhRMA's First Amendment suit is pending and the rule is in effect. Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Utah bar new weight-management incretin prescriptions under 12 and require in-person specialist initiation for 12–17. Four states cap telehealth initial fills at 30 days.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on frozen manufacturer prices. Bridge pilot not revived. The 30% wellness guidance stands. CMS's DXA coverage for 65+ users is the only new benefit, and it treats harm, not access.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Clinic administration records, PBM fills and app logs flow to wellness vendors under consent forms. Clean-panel assays created a new private data stream: scan chains and dating apps hold drug-detection results. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army paused its recruit oral pilot (Aug 2031) after the stress-fracture analysis. TRICARE is unchanged. DOT has issued no rule on drivers' off-label alcohol-reduction use.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: After the Sep 2031 outbreak, India suspended 14 export licences under US pressure, while trade talks still leave mail enforcement unresolved. China's analogue makers gained share in third markets. The US–India price gap is still ~40×. Danish politicians now cite the Danish registries' exocrine finding as much as price.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles US patent litigation with generic semaglutide filers, setting entry no earlier than mid-2033; Lilly and Novo hold TrumpRx prices at 2029 levels, and a Business Group on Health survey later finds only 28% of employers still cover weight loss

FDA approves a 12 mg retatrutide tier showing ~29% average weight loss, under a REMS limiting it to BMI ≥35 with comorbidity, in-person initiation and baseline bone scans for patients 60+; Lilly says supply will be allocated through 2032

CDC links 287 bloodstream and abscess infections, 11 fatal, in 23 states to contaminated semaglutide vials from two Indian export brands sold through social-media shops; India suspends 14 export licences

CDC reports US hip-fracture hospitalisations among adults 65+ rose ~4% since 2028, the first rise in decades, largely among incretin users; days later FDA rejects Lilly's bid to extend tirzepatide's dementia claim to older adults without heart disease, citing fracture risk
HHS rule ends broadcast advertising for obesity drugs as PhRMA sues; Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Utah enact laws barring weight-loss incretin prescriptions for children under 12

FDA adds 'emotional blunting' to incretin labels after its 118,000-patient study finds dose-related anhedonia; large employers drop 'steadiness' from competency frameworks as 'clean panel' drug-free blood tests become a premium gym and dating-app badge

open_tensions: Drug holidays and dose-downs are now clinically endorsed for blunting, but adherence-verified tracks still dock the 30% premium differential for a skipped clinic month. The label and the wellness guidance now point in opposite directions for ~5.2M workers.

Prices are frozen until generic semaglutide arrives in 2033 at the earliest, and the REMS floor on retatrutide 12 mg shuts out people below BMI 35. Together they keep feeding an ~8.7M-person gray market a year after a fatal contamination outbreak.

The bone wave is now a public-health statistic, and the oldest and longest-exposed users carry most of it. Lilly's dementia programme, Part D's growing spend and CMS's new DXA benefit all assume these users stay on drug for decades.

Thinness has lost its prestige, and the upper tier performs appetite and 'clean' bodies while often floor-dosing in private. The cheap, thin, soft body has become the mark of the bottom and middle, the people who most rely on the drug.

prose.headline: Thin Got Cheap. Now the Rich Are Buying Their Appetite Back, and Proving It With a Blood Test
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 nearly one American adult in four takes an incretin drug. It got there without getting cheaper. The government cash channel still sells starter pills at $149 and maintenance at the same $249 it charged in 2029. Novo Nordisk settled its patent fights in a way that keeps generic semaglutide out until 2033. Lilly says it cannot make enough of its strongest product to cut the price. Employers kept leaving: barely more than a quarter still pay for weight loss as such. Most of the rest of the country pays cash, and the rest of that rest buys from the mail.

The strongest product is a higher dose of an old one. Last June the FDA approved a 12-milligram tier of Lilly's retatrutide that takes off close to three-tenths of body weight. That is the territory of surgery, delivered by a weekly pen. The agency fenced it in: a BMI floor, an in-person first prescription, and a bone scan for anyone over sixty. People below the floor found it anyway, as 'reta' research peptide from social shops. Some of those vials held ten times their labelled dose.

The mail has always carried risk, and in September 2031 it carried bacteria. Two Indian export brands of semaglutide, sold through Instagram and Telegram storefronts, produced bloodstream infections in 23 states, and eleven people died. India suspended fourteen export licences under American pressure. Other brands replaced them within a season. Close to nine million Americans now take product the FDA has not approved, most of them in the bottom two income thirds.

The bones were the larger story, because they move slowly and count everyone. In November the CDC reported that hip-fracture hospitalisations among older Americans had risen for the first time in decades, and that the excess sat mostly among drug users. That fits a decade of losing muscle along with fat and, for the longest users, a pancreas that has stopped absorbing the vitamins bone needs. The same month the FDA refused to extend tirzepatide's dementia-prevention claim to older adults without heart disease, citing fractures. Medicare now pays for bone scans for users over 65. Gyms have contracts with Medicare Advantage plans to teach grandmothers deadlifts.

The mood finding settled into ordinary life. In May the FDA added emotional blunting to every label after its own study found it in about one user in twelve, more at high doses. Nobody was surprised; 'going flat' had been a sitcom premise for a year. Dose-downs and holidays are what doctors now recommend, and most big companies quietly deleted 'steadiness' from their competency language. The adherence tracks did not change. Workers in the Columbus-corridor warehouses who skip a monthly clinic shot to feel like themselves at a wedding still lose their premium discount.

The states that acted, acted to restrict. Five Southern and Mountain West legislatures barred weight-loss prescriptions for children under twelve. HHS took obesity drugs off television, over a pending industry lawsuit. No legislature acted on cost.

As thinness became cheap, it stopped meaning much. In Brooklyn and Silver Lake, the prestige body is now a fed one: muscled, a little heavy, eating bread at a long table. For $180, a blood test shows no peptide in it. Dating apps sell the 'clean panel' badge to premium members. Some of the women posting their results are floor-dosing between tests. The thin, soft body that shows up at the warehouse clinic every month carries no status at all. Seen from a distance the country is thinner than ever, and the people at the top have started treating thinness as a sign of being poor.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marcus Bell, 44, badges into the Groveport fulfilment centre at 5:52 and goes to the clinic trailer before his shift, because it is the third Thursday. The nurse scans his wrist, then asks the new questions off a tablet: any loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, on a scale of one to five. He says two. She types two.

"Rhonda wants me off for the anniversary," he says.

"Then you skip October. That's your call." She doesn't look up. "Benefits will see it."

Benefits will see it as $212 a month. He rolls his sleeve.

At lunch he eats half a chicken box and gives the rest to Dez, who is checking a vial's lot number against an FDA list on his phone, the way everyone has since September. "Clean," Dez says, meaning not on the list.

On break Marcus scrolls past a woman in a Brooklyn kitchen tearing a baguette, butter on her chin, a lab printout taped to the fridge behind her. CLEAN PANEL, the caption says. 11 months natty. His daughter Kayla, eleven, has liked it.

At home Rhonda has made lasagna. He eats a square and feels nothing about it, which is the same as feeling fine. Kayla asks if she can have seconds and Rhonda says yes too quickly.

The television runs a car ad, a phone ad, a sportsbook ad. No pens anymore. Rhonda turns the anniversary card over on the counter so he can see the date she has circled.

"One month," she says.

He does the subtraction in his head: $212 for the month.
